cognito_allowed_client_ids.description: App client ids accepted as valid callers by the CUSTOM_JWT authorizer.

cognito_required_custom_claims.description:
Required custom claims the Gateway CUSTOM_JWT authorizer must find on an
inbound token, e.g. `[{claim_name = "custom:rep_id", required_value = ""}]`
is not meaningful (a fixed required_value only supports EQUALS matches
against a known value, not "claim is present with any value") — callers
needing presence-only enforcement should rely on the interceptor's own
`decode_identity` rejection instead and leave this list empty; it exists
for claims that must equal one fixed value across every caller (e.g. a
fixed `token_use` or `principal_type` claim).

ecr_repository_name.description: Name of the ECR repository holding the agent container image.

Content hash of the agent source tree (e.g. computed by the root

`data "archive_file"` resource's `output_base64sha256`), used purely as

tags.description: Resource tags. The provider's default_tags already covers the five mandatory tags; this allows a per-resource override or addition.

tool_lambda_arns.description:
Map of tool_name -> that tool's action Lambda ARN
(`module.lambda_action[tool_name].function_arn`), one entry per tool in
`crm.toolspec.definitions.ALL_TOOLS`. Every gateway target in this module
is generated from this map's `for_each` — a target cannot exist without a
matching Lambda ARN, and every entry produces exactly one target. Must
carry exactly 24 entries. Deliberately one more than the `api` module's 23
routes: `get_page_context` is reachable by the agents and the Gateway but
has no HTTP route (`local.agent_only_tools` in `infra/main.tf`).

tool_schemas.description:
Map of tool_name -> that tool's flattened MCP tool schema, required by the
provider's `aws_bedrockagentcore_gateway_target` resource
(`target_configuration.mcp.lambda.tool_schema` is a required block — a
target cannot be created without one). Must carry the same 22 keys as
`tool_lambda_arns`.

Each entry's `description` and `properties` are derived by the root
composition from `crm.toolspec.definitions.ALL_TOOLS[tool_name]`
(`.description` and the top-level keys of `.input_schema["properties"]`),
not hand-copied — the same source `render_mcp_tools()` generates the MCP
tool surface from, so the Gateway's declared schema cannot silently drift
from the Lambda's own `input_schema` validation.

Only top-level, scalar-typed properties are expressible directly; a
property whose JSON Schema type is itself `object` or `array` needs a
nested `items_json`/`properties_json` string (see the provider schema
under `input_schema.property.{items_json,properties_json}`) that this
variable's shape does not carry — every one of the 22 tools' top-level
input properties in `crm.toolspec.definitions` is scalar (`string`,
`number`, `boolean`) or a simple array of scalars represented as `type =
"array"` with no nested object items, so this limitation does not affect
any tool in this project's toolspec today; a future tool with a nested
object/array property would need this variable's shape extended before
it could be represented here.

access_log_group_name.description: CloudWatch Logs group name receiving API Gateway access logs.

api_endpoint.description: HTTP API's default execution endpoint (`https://<api-id>.execute-api.<region>.amazonaws.com`). Reachable directly, in addition to any CloudFront behaviour placed in front of it — see the README's `execute-api` note.

authorizer_id.description: Cognito JWT authorizer id — every route in this module references this one authorizer; exposed for the Layer 3 gate's authorizer-coverage assertion.

execution_arn.description: API execution ARN, for Lambda resource-policy `source_arn` patterns outside this module if needed.

route_tool_names.description: Sorted list of the 22 tool names this module generated routes for, derived from `var.tool_lambda_invoke_arns`'s keys — for the Layer 3 gate to diff against `crm.toolspec.definitions.ALL_TOOLS`.

stage_invoke_url.description: Full invoke URL for the deployed stage. For a private API this is reachable only from inside the VPC through a named interface endpoint — it is NOT a publicly callable URL, and a smoke check that reaches it from outside the VPC has not tested this API.

cognito_issuer_url.description: Cognito user pool issuer URL (`https://cognito-idp.<region>.amazonaws.com/<user_pool_id>`), used as the JWT authorizer's issuer.

(`module.lambda_action[tool_name].invoke_arn`), one entry per tool in

every integration, and every authorizer attachment is generated from — see
`main.tf`'s `for_each` over this map. Must carry exactly 22 entries.

mcp_client_id.description: App client id for MCP clients (confidential client).

This instantiation's rows in the project-wide table × action × role matrix,

api_gateway_execution_arn.description: The API Gateway REST/HTTP API execution ARN pattern (`arn:aws:execute-api:<region>:<account>:<api-id>/*`) permitted to invoke this function via its resource policy.

dynamodb_grants.description:
Least-privilege per-table DynamoDB IAM grants for this function's execution
role. Each entry names one table (or one table's index) and the exact actions
permitted on it — never `dynamodb:*` and never `Resource = "*"`. Both halves
are rejected by the validation blocks below: two constrain `actions`, two
constrain `table_arn` and `index_arns`.

`leading_key_condition` is optional and applies **only** where the table's
partition key genuinely encodes the caller's own identity (e.g. `reps`,
keyed by `rep_id`). For the four synthetic-id entity tables (`accounts`,
`contacts`, `opportunities`, `activities`), the partition key is the
record's own generated id, not the rep id, so a `LeadingKeys` condition
there would reference an attribute the policy engine cannot correlate to
the caller and would silently never match. Rep-scoped isolation for those four tables is
enforced in application code (`crm.authz`), not in this IAM grant; this
module does not fabricate a `LeadingKeys` condition against a
non-rep-keyed table regardless of what a caller passes here — see
`table_action_role_matrix.json` for the authoritative disposition per
table.

environment_kms_key_arn.description: KMS customer-managed key ARN used to encrypt the function's environment variables. Required whenever `environment_variables` carries anything sensitive; the module does not guess — callers with no sensitive env vars may omit it (encryption then falls back to the AWS-managed Lambda default).

environment_variables.description: Plaintext environment variables for the function. Anything sensitive must instead be a Secrets Manager / SSM Parameter Store reference resolved at runtime, never an inline secret value.

filename.description: Path to the zipped deployment package for this function.

function_name.description: Unique Lambda function name. Also names this instantiation's dedicated IAM role, log group, and CloudWatch alarms.

gateway_target_role_arn.description:
The AgentCore Gateway target execution role ARN permitted to invoke this function via its resource
policy — the sole non-API-Gateway principal ever admitted for a CRM tool. `null`
declares no such permission, for a function that is not a Gateway target.

log_retention_days.description: Explicit CloudWatch Logs retention for this function's log group.

reserved_concurrent_executions.description:
Reserved concurrency for this function. MUST be greater than zero: a value of
0 does not merely "throttle" the function, it makes the function permanently
uninvokable (every invocation is throttled with no path to succeed), which is
a silent brick rather than a limit. There is no valid reason for an action
Lambda behind API Gateway to declare 0 here, so the module rejects it at plan
time via the validation block below rather than deferring to a live check.

Callers are also responsible for keeping the sum of every instantiation's
reserved concurrency, across the whole deployment, below the account's total
concurrency pool (1,000 by default) minus whatever headroom the root
composition reserves for unreserved/on-demand invocations. This module cannot
see its sibling instantiations, so it cannot enforce the sum itself; the root
composition and the consolidated Layer 3 gate own that check.

source_code_hash.description: Base64-encoded SHA256 of the deployment package, forcing redeploy on code change.

table_action_role_matrix_entries.description:
This instantiation's rows in the project-wide table × action × role matrix.
Each entry documents, for one (table, action) pair this
function is granted, whether `dynamodb:LeadingKeys` genuinely enforces rep
isolation here or whether isolation is enforced in application code instead.
Purely documentary — asserted against by the consolidated Layer 3 gate, not
read at plan time by this module — but required so the matrix is
machine-readable per instantiation rather than assembled by hand afterward.

isolation here or whether isolation is enforced in application code instead.
Purely documentary — asserted against by the consolidated Layer 3 gate, not
read at plan time by this module — but required so the matrix is
machine-readable per instantiation rather than assembled by hand afterward.

role_arn.description: This instantiation's dedicated execution role ARN.

role_name.description: This instantiation's dedicated execution role name — never shared with any other instantiation.

table_action_role_matrix_rows.description:
This instantiation's rows in the project-wide table × action × role matrix,
with `role` filled in from the actual generated role
name. The root composition collects every instantiation's rows (via
`flatten([for m in module.lambda_action : m.table_action_role_matrix_rows])`)
into one machine-readable file for the consolidated Layer 3 gate to assert
against.

api_gateway_execution_arn.description: The API Gateway REST/HTTP API execution ARN pattern (`arn:aws:execute-api:<region>:<account>:<api-id>/*`) permitted to invoke this function via its resource policy.

dynamodb_grants.description:
Least-privilege per-table DynamoDB IAM grants for this function's execution
role. Each entry names one table (or one table's index) and the exact actions
permitted on it — never `dynamodb:*` and never `Resource = "*"`. Both halves
are rejected by the validation blocks below: two constrain `actions`, two
constrain `table_arn` and `index_arns`.

`leading_key_condition` is optional and applies **only** where the table's
partition key genuinely encodes the caller's own identity (e.g. `reps`,
keyed by `rep_id`). For the four synthetic-id entity tables (`accounts`,
`contacts`, `opportunities`, `activities`), the partition key is the
record's own generated id, not the rep id, so a `LeadingKeys` condition
there would reference an attribute the policy engine cannot correlate to
the caller and would silently never match. Rep-scoped isolation for those four tables is
enforced in application code (`crm.authz`), not in this IAM grant; this
module does not fabricate a `LeadingKeys` condition against a
non-rep-keyed table regardless of what a caller passes here — see
`table_action_role_matrix.json` for the authoritative disposition per
table.

environment_kms_key_arn.description: KMS customer-managed key ARN used to encrypt the function's environment variables. Required whenever `environment_variables` carries anything sensitive; the module does not guess — callers with no sensitive env vars may omit it (encryption then falls back to the AWS-managed Lambda default).

environment_variables.description: Plaintext environment variables for the function. Anything sensitive must instead be a Secrets Manager / SSM Parameter Store reference resolved at runtime, never an inline secret value.

filename.description: Path to the zipped deployment package for this function.

function_name.description: Unique Lambda function name. Also names this instantiation's dedicated IAM role, log group, and CloudWatch alarms.

gateway_target_role_arn.description:
The AgentCore Gateway target execution role ARN permitted to invoke this function via its resource
policy — the sole non-API-Gateway principal ever admitted for a CRM tool. `null`
declares no such permission, for a function that is not a Gateway target.

log_retention_days.description: Explicit CloudWatch Logs retention for this function's log group.

reserved_concurrent_executions.description:
Reserved concurrency for this function. MUST be greater than zero: a value of
0 does not merely "throttle" the function, it makes the function permanently
uninvokable (every invocation is throttled with no path to succeed), which is
a silent brick rather than a limit. There is no valid reason for an action
Lambda behind API Gateway to declare 0 here, so the module rejects it at plan
time via the validation block below rather than deferring to a live check.

Callers are also responsible for keeping the sum of every instantiation's
reserved concurrency, across the whole deployment, below the account's total
concurrency pool (1,000 by default) minus whatever headroom the root
composition reserves for unreserved/on-demand invocations. This module cannot
see its sibling instantiations, so it cannot enforce the sum itself; the root
composition and the consolidated Layer 3 gate own that check.

source_code_hash.description: Base64-encoded SHA256 of the deployment package, forcing redeploy on code change.

eval_metric_namespace.description: CloudWatch custom metric namespace reserved for eval-run metrics. Passthrough of `var.eval_metric_namespace` — see that variable's description for the `src/eval/` investigation this value is based on.

description.constant_value: CMK for CloudTrail S3 log destination encryption at rest
CMK for CloudWatch Logs log group encryption at rest

cloudtrail_s3_log_retention_days.description:
Lifecycle expiration, in days, for CloudTrail's delivered log objects in
the trail's S3 destination bucket. Kept separate from
`log_retention_days` (CloudWatch Logs retention) because the two live in
different services with different cost profiles; 365 days matches a
one-year audit-trail expectation for API activity history.

data_classification.description: Value for the `data-classification` tag on resources in this module.

enable_cloudtrail_cloudwatch_logs.description:
Whether the trail also delivers to a CloudWatch Logs log group (via
`cloud_watch_logs_group_arn`/`cloud_watch_logs_role_arn`), in addition to
its mandatory S3 destination. Off by default: `sa-agent` flagged
CloudTrail cost as a Warning, and the CloudWatch Logs delivery path adds
per-GB CloudWatch Logs ingestion/storage charges on top of the S3
destination's near-free storage, for a control (fast searchability of
trail events) this build does not need at v1 — S3 + Athena/CloudTrail
Lake is the query path if ever needed. Enabling this later requires no
other change to this module; the CMK this module creates already grants
`logs.<region>.amazonaws.com` the actions CloudWatch Logs needs.

eval_metric_namespace.description:
CloudWatch custom metric namespace reserved for eval-run metrics. No code
under `src/` publishes a CloudWatch metric; eval metrics are written to the
`matrix.json`/`.md`/`.csv` report files instead.

log_retention_days.description:
Explicit CloudWatch Logs retention, in days, for the CloudTrail
CloudWatch Logs integration log group this module creates. 90 days covers a
quarterly access review without the "never expire" default.

Local filesystem directory containing one pre-built zip per Lambda
function this composition deploys (22 tool Lambdas, the identity
interceptor, and the pre-token-generation trigger), named
`<function-key>.zip`. Declared here rather than in `infra/variables.tf`
(owned by an earlier task) because it is specific to this composition's
